title: Breaking the quadratic color bound for bounded outdegree
formal: Do there exist a constant \(\varepsilon \in\)(0,1], constants \(C_{1},C_{2}>0, a\) computable function \(f:\mathbb{N} _{+}\to \mathbb{N} _{+}\) and one deterministic LOCAL algorithm that, for every n-vertex graph supplied with an orientation of maximum outdegree at most \(\beta \ge 1\), computes a proper vertex coloring using at most \(\lceil C_{1}\beta ^{2- \varepsilon}\rceil\) colors within \(f(\beta )+C_{2}\log * n\) rounds?
context:
The orientation controls how many edges leave a vertex, not how many neighbors it has. Thus a fast coloring theorem parameterized by maximum total degree cannot simply replace \(\beta\) here.

Linial’s result, as recalled in the source, gives \(O(\beta ^{2})\) colors in \(O(\log * n)\) rounds. The question asks for a fixed positive reduction in the exponent while allowing extra time depending only on \(\beta\).

Graphs with this orientation admit \(O(\beta )\)-colorings. The source records an \(O(\beta )\)-coloring algorithm with a multiplicative logarithmic dependence on n, which misses the requested additive \(f(\beta )+O(\log * n)\) regime.

The August 2026 preprint obtains stronger oriented list-defective guarantees and a proper-list-coloring result with lists of size \(\beta ^{2}+\beta +1\). That does not provide the subquadratic exponent asked for here.
why: Would cross a basic locality barrier for coloring sparse oriented networks, making fewer colors achievable without paying global-size-dependent time beyond \(\log * n\).
status_note: The complete source question, deterministic LOCAL conventions and August 2026 oriented-list theorem were checked. Later searches did not locate the stated uniform subquadratic palette guarantee through 12 September 2026.

progress.text: The source isolates subquadratic proper coloring in \(f(\beta )+O(\log * n)\) rounds as open, despite advances in list and defective variants.
New oriented list-defective results include proper list coloring at quadratic list size; they do not give the requested fixed exponent improvement.

sentences: The network comes with an orientation having at most \(\beta\) outgoing edges at every vertex.
A deterministic distributed algorithm can already color it with \(O(\beta ^{2})\) colors in \(O(\log * n)\) rounds.
The question is whether \(\beta ^{2}\) can be replaced by \(\beta ^{2- \varepsilon}\) for one fixed \(\varepsilon >0\).
Additional time may depend arbitrarily on \(\beta\), but the dependence on n must remain additive \(O(\log * n)\).
New results for list and defective colorings have not supplied this proper-coloring guarantee.

definitions: The communication network is a finite undirected simple graph \(G=(V,E), |V|=n\ge 2\). Every edge has a supplied direction, known to its endpoints; no acyclicity is promised. A vertex’s outdegree is its number of outgoing edges, and every vertex has outdegree at most the supplied bound \(\beta\). Its indegree and total degree may be arbitrarily large. A proper coloring assigns each vertex a label from one common palette so that endpoints of every edge have different labels, regardless of the edge direction. Vertices execute the same deterministic algorithm in synchronous rounds, have unique identifiers of \(O(\log  n)\) bits, know their incident ports and edge directions, and may know n and \(\beta\). Each round allows a separate message of unbounded size to each neighbor in either direction and unrestricted finite local computation. Cost is worst-case round count over graphs, orientations and identifiers. No precomputed coloring or graph decomposition is supplied. The function f may grow arbitrarily fast with \(\beta\), but cannot depend on n, total degree or the orientation’s path lengths. Both the exponent improvement \(\varepsilon\) and the coefficient of \(\log * n\) must be uniform over \(\beta\) and n. Here \(\log * n\) is the number of repeated base-two logarithms needed to reach a value at most one. Edgeless graphs, including the \(\beta =0\) case, can be assigned one color separately.
answer_criterion: Prove the existence of the uniform deterministic algorithm with the stated palette and additive round bound, or establish that no such \(\varepsilon\), constants, computable f and algorithm exist. A palette reduction by only logarithmic factors, a runtime depending on total degree, or a multiplicative log n term does not establish this claim.
